role: Senior Analyst / Manager of Data & Analytics
responsibilities: Insights & Recommendations: Partner with cross-functional teams and senior stakeholders to understand business questions, deliver timely analysis, and surface opportunities for data-driven improvement
Visualizations & Dashboarding: Design and maintain ad-hoc and recurring Looker reports; build and monitor key business metrics; proactively identify trends and performance gaps
Data Modeling: Build, optimize, and document LookML models that support scalable, efficient analysis across the organization

Infrastructure & Data Quality: Audit existing dashboards and data sources to identify consolidation opportunities; diagnose and resolve data discrepancies; partner with the Data Engineering team to improve data pipelines and ensure reporting accuracy. Possess a strong instinct for when data doesn't look right and the analytical rigor to trace issues back to their source.
Predictive Modeling: Develop and maintain models that forecast business outcomes, customer behavior, and other key metrics
Subject Matter Expertise: Develop deep familiarity with SoulCycle's full data landscape and contribute to evolving how the business measures performance

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: knows how to prioritize competing demands without losing rigor or quality
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Rigour: quality vocabulary outnumbers speed vocabulary roughly two to one — 'without losing rigor or quality', 'ensure reporting accuracy', 'the analytical rigor to trace issues back to their source', 'detail-obsessed'.
evidence.domain_risk: Develop and maintain models that forecast business outcomes, customer behavior, and other key metrics
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Moderate: the work informs commercial decisions for a consumer fitness brand, with no financial-reporting, audit or regulatory language anywhere in the JD.
evidence.data_team_maturity: partner with the Data Engineering team to improve data pipelines and ensure reporting accuracy
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Mid: Looker and LookML are already in production and a separate Data Engineering team exists, but the role is still asked to 'help build a culture of data-driven decision-making across the organization'.
evidence.jd_authorship: Data Modeling: Build, optimize, and document LookML models that support scalable, efficient analysis across the organization
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Hiring manager: the bullets name the actual tools and the actual mess — 'Build, optimize, and document LookML models' and 'Audit existing dashboards and data sources to identify consolidation opportunities'.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Develop and maintain models that forecast business outcomes, customer behavior, and other key metrics
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: Commercial: the analysis serves business performance and customer behaviour for the wider company — 'help SoulCycle make smarter, faster decisions' — rather than a product, finance or data-platform audience.
evidence.autonomy_level: contribute to our long-term data strategy
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Mixed: the role owns the LookML modelling layer outright while the surrounding framing is service-oriented — 'Partner with cross-functional teams and senior stakeholders... deliver timely analysis'.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: None: the JD makes no mention of AI, LLMs or AI-assisted tooling in either responsibilities or qualifications.
evidence.testing_framing: diagnose and resolve data discrepancies; partner with the Data Engineering team to improve data pipelines and ensure reporting accuracy
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Responsibility: 'Infrastructure & Data Quality' is its own responsibility heading with ownership verbs, not a testing tool listed under qualifications.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Possess a strong instinct for when data doesn't look right and the analytical rigor to trace issues back to their source.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Moderate: accuracy is a genuine concern — catching data that 'doesn't look right' before it is used — but it occupies one bullet of six and carries no compliance or regulatory weight.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Audit existing dashboards and data sources to identify consolidation opportunities
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Fix/scale: the infrastructure work is consolidation and repair — 'Audit existing dashboards', 'diagnose and resolve data discrepancies', 'improve data pipelines' — not building something new.
evidence.loss_aversion: Risk framing centres on catching wrong numbers before they are acted on: 'Possess a strong instinct for when data doesn't look right and the analytical rigor to trace issues back to their source.'
